official.application_cycle: 2027 scholarship round; the internship itself runs July to September 2027
official.status_note: The Ministry's page states "Applications for the 2027 New Zealand Space Scholarship open on 1 October 2026" and carries a live "Apply now" link into MBIE's recruitment system. No closing date is published for the round.
benefits: Return economy flights to the United States
Reasonable travel-related expenses, including insurance support where applicable
Hands-on experience on space missions and science projects alongside JPL scientists and engineers
Skills and networks that support future careers in New Zealand's space and advanced aviation sectors
eligibility: Be a New Zealand citizen (NASA requirement)
Be enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities
Hold a minimum GPA equivalent of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (New Zealand grades must be converted to the US GPA scale)
Be proficient in written and spoken English (NASA requirement)
Be available to undertake the internship in person from July to September 2027, be eligible for a J1 or F1 visa, and be able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance
requirements: Nominate up to 2 research areas that best match your studies
Provide proof of enrolment in postgraduate study at a New Zealand tertiary institution before the scholarship is awarded, if completing your current qualification before 2027
Follow the participant code of conduct and arrange appropriate travel and medical insurance
Participate in promotional, outreach and alumni activities
documents: Proof of enrolment in postgraduate study at a New Zealand tertiary institution (for applicants completing their current qualification before 2027)
selection_criteria: Relevance of experience to JPL projects
Commitment to contributing to JPL and New Zealand's space sector
coverage: Return economy flights to the United States
Reasonable travel-related expenses, including insurance support where applicable
Costs associated with participating in the internship only - any additional expenses remain the responsibility of the recipient
application_method: Apply online through the "Apply now" link on the New Zealand Space Scholarship page, which opens an application in MBIE's recruitment system
Nominate up to 2 research areas that best match your studies
official.application_route: Apply online via the "Apply now" link on MBIE's New Zealand Space Scholarship page, which routes to MBIE's recruitment (SuccessFactors) application form.
official.citizenship_residency: New Zealand citizenship is required (a NASA requirement)
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution, in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities
official.research_requirement: Applicants are asked to nominate up to 2 research areas that best match their studies; possible areas include advanced aviation, AI/machine learning and advanced computing, astrobiology and biology, astrophysics and space science, autonomy and robotics, deep space communications, Earth observation and Earth science, instrument and sensor development, planetary science, and science and space communication.
official.duration: 3-month internship, July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
official.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students the opportunity to undertake a fully supported 3-month internship at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, working alongside leading scientists and engineers on cutting-edge space missions and research. The initiative seeks to better prepare students for future careers in the New Zealand space and advanced aviation sectors.
official.program_type: Scholarship for a fully supported 3-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (not a degree programme)
official.english_requirement: Be proficient in written and spoken English (NASA requirement); no test score is published.

verification.notes: Live MBIE page (last updated 1 October 2026) publishes the covered cost categories and the eligibility rules but no monetary figure and no closing date for the 2027 round; the "Apply now" link routes to MBIE's recruitment system.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a three-month paid internship placement at NASA JPL, not a degree scholarship, so the value arrives as flights, accommodation and a daily living allowance rather than a single bursary figure - budget for the gap between the allowance and Southern California living costs yourself. Because MBIE shortlists and then hands its shortlist to JPL for the final decision, the strength of your match to a specific JPL project area matters more than your GPA once you clear the 3.0 threshold. Start your enrolment proof and visa paperwork early: the Ministry requires evidence that you will be or already are enrolled in postgraduate STEM study at a New Zealand institution before the award is made.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New Zealand citizen postgraduate STEM students with a 3.0+ GPA on the US 4.0 scale who can be in Southern California in person for the whole of July to September 2027.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold New Zealand citizenship only - check your status against NASA's Designated Countries List, since holding or having held citizenship of a listed country disqualifies you outright
Convert your New Zealand grades to the US 4.0 GPA scale and confirm you are at or above 3.0 before you start the form
Pick your two research areas from the Ministry's published list and write them so they map onto a plausible JPL project rather than your thesis title
If you will finish your current qualification before 2027, secure a written offer or enrolment pathway from a New Zealand tertiary institution now
Budget for travel and medical insurance, visa costs and any additional expenses the allowance will not reach
common_rejection_risks: Failing the NASA Designated Countries List exclusion through dual or former citizenship - this is checked before anything else and is not waivable
Nominating research areas that do not line up with JPL's current mission priorities, so the shortlist never reaches a JPL reviewer who wants you
Being under the 3.0 GPA threshold once grades are converted to the US scale, which is stricter than it looks for New Zealand B/B+ averages
Being unable to prove postgraduate enrolment at a New Zealand institution before the award is made, which stalls the application at the last step
Not being able to commit to the full in-person July to September 2027 window because of teaching, fieldwork or another placement
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any expense beyond the internship itself: MBIE states the scholarship only covers costs associated with participating in the internship and that additional expenses remain the recipient's responsibility, so visa fees, insurance excesses, personal spending and anything outside the published categories sit with you.
document_audit: The only document the Ministry names is proof of postgraduate enrolment at a New Zealand tertiary institution - and it must exist before the award, not before the deadline
Your academic record will be read on the US GPA scale, so supply the conversion rather than leaving JPL to guess
No closing date is published, so do not assume the round stays open until an advertised finish; contact the New Zealand Space Agency if you need certainty
alerts: The 2027 round opened on 1 October 2026 and the Ministry publishes no closing date - treat the window as short
MBIE assessment is not the final word: final shortlisted candidates are submitted to JPL for final selection
Applicants who hold or have held citizenship of a country on NASA's Designated Countries List are not eligible at all
Recipients take on participant code of conduct, insurance and outreach obligations - these are conditions, not suggestions
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online through the MBIE recruitment link, nominate your two research areas, then MBIE assesses and forwards its shortlist to JPL, which makes the final selection.
